title: Data-driven Rural Interventions for Vitality and Endurance Pilot Study
official: Data-driven Rural Interventions for Vitality and Endurance Pilot Study
summary:
The study aims to explore whether data driven, personalized wellness interventions-based on integrated genomic, clinical, behavioral, and functional data- are feasible in a rural facing setting and can produce measurable improvements in cardiometabolic, cognitive, mental health, and functional wellness outcomes within four months.

This study has three primary goals.

1. Identify scientific, behavioral, operational, and institutional learnings to inform future, larger-scale precision health research.
2. Explore how data from diverse rural populations can contribute to understanding diseases and resilience factors across environments.
3. Build frameworks for scalable community engagement, data collection, and feedback models.
criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* Adults \>18 years of age or older at enrollment ● Weight is greater than or equal to 110 lbs
* Able and willing to comprehend and sign the informed consent document
* Able and willing to perform required physical performance tests
* Able and willing to provide study samples
* Able and willing to participate in study procedures
* Able and willing to complete surveys, cognitive assessments, and questionnaires in English only
* Able and willing to wear a fitness tracker as continuously as possible for the duration of the study.

Weissman Hood Institute at Touro University Protocol # MRI010 Data-driven Rural Interventions for Vitality and Endurance (DRIVE) Pilot page 5 of 36

● Has or has ready access to a PC, tablet, or smartphone with an internet connection required for procedures that they consent to

Exclusion Criteria:

* A diagnosis of dementia
* Self-reported pregnancy or breastfeeding
* Individuals not fluent in written and spoken English
* Self-reported chronic or end-stage disease that would interfere with their participation in the study
* Severe and non-correctable hearing and visual impairment that would interfere with the ability to complete study measures
* Individuals for whom the total volume of blood would exceed 550 mL over an 8-week period and/or more than two draws within one week for combined clinical and research purposes. ● Any other vulnerable subject at the time of enrollment as specified above
